cues.zh: 本视频由 Lutron 的 Kaseta 赞助。

cues.en: According to the general theory of relativity,
cues.zh: 根据广义相对论，

cues.en: gravity is not a force. There are no gravitational fields.
cues.zh: 引力并不是一种力，引力场也并不存在。

cues.en: Gravity is kind of an illusion.
cues.zh: 引力在某种程度上只是一种错觉。

cues.en: And in this video, I will prove it to you by blasting off into outer space.
cues.zh: 在今天的视频里，我将飞向外太空来向你证明这一点。

cues.en: In three,
cues.zh: 倒数三、

cues.en: two, one.
cues.zh: 二、一。

cues.en: Albert Einstein said the happiest thought of his life was imagining
cues.zh: 爱因斯坦曾说，他一生中最快乐的思考，是想象

cues.en: a man falling off the roof of a house.
cues.zh: 一个人从屋顶摔下来的情景。

cues.en: What made Einstein so happy about this wasn't Schadenfreude.
cues.zh: 让爱因斯坦如此开心的并不是幸灾乐祸，

cues.en: It was the realization
cues.zh: 而是他意识到：

cues.en: that this man, while he was falling,
cues.zh: 这个人在下落的过程中，

cues.en: wouldn't feel his own weight. He would be weightless.
cues.zh: 其实感受不到自身的重量。他是失重的。

cues.en: And anything he dropped on his way down, well, it would remain stationary relative to him or moving in uniform motion.
cues.zh: 而他在下落途中松开的任何东西，相对于他来说都会保持静止，或是做匀速运动。

cues.en: The whole situation
cues.zh: 这整个情景

cues.en: would be just
cues.zh: 简直就

cues.en: like
cues.zh: 像

cues.en: If
cues.zh: 如果

cues.en: you were in deep space,
cues.zh: 你身处深空之中，

cues.en: not near any large masses,
cues.zh: 远离任何大质量天体，

cues.en: with your spaceship at rest or coasting along at constant velocity.
cues.zh: 飞船保持静止或以恒定速度滑行一样。

cues.en: Here,
cues.zh: 在这里，

cues.en: you would feel no weight.
cues.zh: 你感觉不到任何重量。

cues.en: Objects would remain stationary relative to you, or if you give them a push,
cues.zh: 物体相对于你保持静止，或者只要你推它一把，

cues.en: they would move in a straight line at constant velocity.
cues.zh: 它就会以恒定速度做匀速直线运动。

cues.en: And you would be the very definition of an inertial observer.
cues.zh: 而这正是惯性观察者的标准定义。

cues.en: You're not accelerating,
cues.zh: 你没有在加速，

cues.en: not in a gravitational field. All the laws of physics apply in your reference frame.
cues.zh: 也不在引力场中。所有的物理定律在你的参考系中都完全适用。

cues.en: Meaning, there is no experiment you could do to distinguish
cues.zh: 这意味着，你做不出任何实验来区分

cues.en: your inertial reference frame from any other.
cues.zh: 你的惯性参考系和其他惯性参考系。

cues.en: Now, here comes the big leap. Einstein looks at these two scenarios and says, they are equivalent,
cues.zh: 现在，关键的飞跃来了。爱因斯坦审视这两种情景并提出：它们是完全等价的，

cues.en: not just similar.
cues.zh: 而不仅仅是相似。

cues.en: Physically, they are exactly the same thing, which means man falling from roof is not in a gravitational field. There are no gravitational fields.
cues.zh: 从物理上讲，它们完全是一回事，也就是说，从屋顶坠落的人并不处于引力场中。根本不存在引力场。

cues.en: And he is not accelerating.
cues.zh: 而且他也没有在加速。

cues.en: He is an inertial observer just like Rocketman.
cues.zh: 他和“火箭人”一样，都是惯性观察者。

cues.en: Woah. Woah. Woah. I mean, okay. I can see how both of these observers feel weightless,
cues.zh: 哇。哇。哇。我是说，好吧。我能看出这两个观察者都感觉失重，

cues.en: but man falling from roof is clearly in a gravitational field. I mean, he's right next to the Earth,
cues.zh: 但从屋顶坠落的人显然处于引力场中啊。我的意思是，他就在地球旁边，

cues.en: and he's obviously accelerating.
cues.zh: 而且他明显在加速。

cues.en: His speed is increasing by 9.8 meters per second every second, a fact that would become painfully apparent when he crashes into the ground.
cues.zh: 他的速度每秒增加9.8米每秒，等他撞到地面时，这一点会让他痛切体会到。

cues.en: I know that these two situations look very different, but Einstein's equivalence principle tells us the one thing to focus on, the experience of the observer.
cues.zh: 我知道这两种情形看起来非常不同，但爱因斯坦的等效原理告诉我们，只需关注一件事——观察者的体验。

cues.en: If they feel weightless,
cues.zh: 如果他们感觉失重，

cues.en: then they are in an inertial frame of reference. Every bit as good as Rocketman's out drifting through deep space.
cues.zh: 那么他们就处于惯性参考系中，和在深空中漂流的“火箭人”的感受完全一样。

cues.en: Imagine if Rocketman coasting along at constant velocity and not paying attention comes upon a planet a long way off in the distance.
cues.zh: 想象一下，“火箭人”以恒定速度巡航，没太留意，忽然看到远处有一颗行星。

cues.en: An external observer might notice that the path of the rocket bends ever so slightly towards the planet.
cues.zh: 外部观察者可能会注意到，火箭的路径微微朝行星方向弯曲。

cues.en: But inside,
cues.zh: 但在火箭内部，

cues.en: Rocketman would remain
cues.zh: “火箭人”依然

cues.en: oblivious.
cues.zh: 浑然不觉。

cues.en: He feels no force, experiences
cues.zh: 他没有感受到任何力，也体验不到

cues.en: no acceleration.
cues.zh: 任何加速度。

cues.en: As the rocket gets closer to the planet, it goes faster and faster.
cues.zh: 随着火箭越来越接近行星，它的速度越来越快。

cues.en: But Rocketman still feels weightless.
cues.zh: 但“火箭人”依然感觉失重。

cues.en: For him, nothing has changed.
cues.zh: 对他来说，什么都没有改变。

cues.en: So where on this journey would you say the frame of reference changes from inertial to non inertial? An onboard accelerometer would never even register a blip.
cues.zh: 那么，在这段旅程中的哪个时刻，你会说参考系从惯性系变成了非惯性系？机载加速度计甚至完全不会有任何读数。

cues.en: He has continued on his inertial path through space time.
cues.zh: 他一直沿着自己的惯性路径穿过时空。

cues.en: So the logical conclusion is his frame of reference is inertial up until the instant he crashes into the planet.
cues.zh: 所以，合理的结论是：直到他撞上行星的那一刻，他的参考系都一直是惯性系。

cues.en: Okay. So how do you explain the curved path of his rocket without gravitational forces or gravitational fields?
cues.zh: 好。那么，如果没有引力或引力场，该如何解释他的火箭沿曲线飞行的轨迹呢？

cues.en: The answer is curved space time.
cues.zh: 答案是弯曲的时空。

cues.en: First, focus on Rocketman's observation that the whole time he felt like he was moving with constant velocity in a straight line.
cues.zh: 首先，关注一下 Rocketman 的观察：整个过程中，他都觉得自己在以恒定速度沿直线运动。

cues.en: He was moving in a straight line through space time. But space time around massive objects like planets is curved, so that's why his path appeared curved to a distant observer. Now
cues.zh: 他是在时空中沿直线运动。但行星等大质量物体周围的时空是弯曲的，所以从远处观察者看来，他的路径才会呈现弯曲。现在

cues.en: this isn't as unusual as it seems.
cues.zh: 这其实没有看起来那么奇怪。

cues.en: Airplanes, for example, always try to fly the shortest route between cities. Essentially, they just go in a straight line. But since the Earth's surface is curved, the shortest path doesn't look like a straight line.
cues.zh: 例如，飞机总是试图在城市之间选择最短航线。本质上，它们只是在沿直线飞行。但由于地球表面是弯曲的，最短路径看起来并不像直线。

cues.en: These shortest paths over curved surfaces are called geodesics,
cues.zh: 曲面上的这些最短路径称为测地线，

cues.en: and we use that same word, geodesics, for the straight line paths followed by inertial observers through curved space time. Here's another analogy.
cues.zh: 对于惯性观察者在弯曲时空中沿直线运动的路径，我们也使用“测地线”这个词。再来看一个类比。

cues.en: Imagine you and a friend are standing a thousand kilometers apart on the Equator.
cues.zh: 想象一下，你和一位朋友站在赤道上，相距一千公里。

cues.en: Now you both set off due north.
cues.zh: 现在你们俩都朝正北方向出发。

cues.en: Over time, you will come closer together, ultimately bumping into each other at the North Pole.
cues.zh: 随着时间的推移，你们会越来越接近，最终在北极点相撞。

cues.en: It's as though there was a force pushing you together,
cues.zh: 就好像有一种力量把你们推到一起，

cues.en: but you didn't feel a force and your friend didn't feel a force. Gravity
cues.zh: 但你没感觉到力，你的朋友也没感觉到力。引力

cues.en: is just like that force. It doesn't actually exist.
cues.zh: 就像那个力一样。它其实并不存在。

cues.en: The real reason for you coming together was that you were both on straight paths, geodesics,
cues.zh: 你们之所以会走到一起，真正的原因是你们都走在直线路径上，也就是测地线上，

cues.en: on a curved surface.
cues.zh: 只不过是在一个弯曲的表面上。

cues.en: Astronauts
cues.zh: 宇航员

cues.en: on the space station are weightless.
cues.zh: 在空间站上处于失重状态。

cues.en: That means they too are inertial observers traveling on a geodesic.
cues.zh: 这意味着他们同样是沿测地线运动的惯性观察者。

cues.en: But the Earth curves spacetime around
cues.zh: 但地球使周围的时空发生了弯曲，

cues.en: which is why their straight line path appears as a helix.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么他们的直线路径看起来像一条螺旋线。

cues.en: It only looks like a circular orbit if you forget the time dimension.
cues.zh: 只有当你忽略时间维度时，它看起来才像一个圆形轨道。

cues.en: Don't forget, we are all moving through space and time.
cues.zh: 别忘了，我们都在空间和时间中运动。

cues.en: Space time.
cues.zh: 时空。

cues.en: This is the standard bent sheet analogy for curved space time, but I think this demo is misleading.
cues.zh: 这是展示弯曲时空的标准“弯曲薄膜”类比，但我认为这个演示有误导性。

cues.en: It allows you to fool yourself into thinking you understand general relativity
cues.zh: 它会让你自以为理解了广义相对论，

cues.en: when the intuition you're actually drawing on is just that objects like to fall towards the middle of a well due to the gravitational force.
cues.zh: 而你实际依靠的直觉，不过是物体在引力作用下喜欢朝凹陷中心掉落罢了。

cues.en: But in general relativity, there is no gravitational force.
cues.zh: 但在广义相对论中，根本不存在引力这种力。

cues.en: What you should be thinking about is objects traveling on a straight line path through space time. It just so happens that space time is curved around massive objects.
cues.zh: 你应该想的是：物体沿着直线穿过时空，只是时空恰好在大质量天体周围是弯曲的。

cues.en: So that straight line path doesn't look like a straight line.
cues.zh: 所以那条直线路径看起来并不像直线。

cues.en: Matter tells space time how to curve,
cues.zh: 物质告诉时空如何弯曲，

cues.en: and space time tells matter how to move.
cues.zh: 时空告诉物质如何运动。

cues.en: Now let's go back to deep space.
cues.zh: 现在让我们回到深空。

cues.en: What happens if you turn on the rocket thrusters and accelerate at 9.8 meters per second squared?
cues.zh: 如果你打开火箭推进器，以9.8米每二次方秒加速，会发生什么？

cues.en: Well, someone outside would see all objects remain stationary,
cues.zh: 嗯，外面的人会看到所有物体保持静止，

cues.en: while the floor of the rocket accelerates
cues.zh: 而火箭的地板加速

cues.en: into them.
cues.zh: 撞向它们。

cues.en: Inside the rocket, everything would appear to accelerate down to the ground,
cues.zh: 在火箭内部，一切看起来都会加速落向地面，

cues.en: and you would feel a force pushing up on your feet,
cues.zh: 你会感到有一股力向上推你的脚，

cues.en: the same force that's pushing up on you as you watch this video.
cues.zh: 和你看这个视频时向上推你的力一样。

cues.en: This situation feels exactly the same as being at rest on the surface of Earth.
cues.zh: 这种情况感觉和静止在地球表面完全相同。

cues.en: Because we are at rest on the surface of Earth.
cues.zh: 因为我们确实静止在地球表面。

cues.en: Now I wanna ask you, are you watching this video in an inertial frame of reference?
cues.zh: 现在我想问你，你是在惯性参考系里看这个视频吗？

cues.en: Well, I mean, do you feel weightless?
cues.zh: 嗯，我是说，你感到失重吗？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 没有。

cues.en: So you are not an inertial observer.
cues.zh: 所以你不是惯性观察者。

cues.en: Your situation is exactly the same as someone accelerating on a rocket ship in deep space.
cues.zh: 你的情况和在深空中乘坐火箭加速的人完全相同。

cues.en: And let me be clear. I don't mean that being at rest in a gravitational field is like accelerating in a rocket. I mean, it is the exact same thing.
cues.zh: 让我说清楚。我不是说在引力场中静止就像在火箭中加速。我是说，这完全是一回事。

cues.en: You are accelerating,
cues.zh: 你在加速，

cues.en: and there is no gravitational field. Gravitational fields do not exist.
cues.zh: 而且不存在引力场。引力场并不存在。

cues.en: Now I know that sounds crazy,
cues.zh: 我知道这听起来很疯狂，

cues.en: but come with me for a minute.
cues.zh: 但先听我讲一会儿。

cues.en: This is you.
cues.zh: 这是你。

cues.en: In standard Newtonian physics, we draw your weight force,
cues.zh: 在标准牛顿物理学中，我们画出你的重力，

cues.en: the force of gravity pushing you down, and the normal force from the floor pushing you up. We say these forces are equal and opposite, so there's no net force on you, so you are not accelerating.
cues.zh: 引力向下推你，地板的支持力向上推你。我们说这些力大小相等、方向相反，所以你受到的合力为零，所以你没有加速。

cues.en: But in general relativity,
cues.zh: 但在广义相对论中，

cues.en: gravity is not a force.
cues.zh: 引力并不是一种力。

cues.en: You have no weight, so the only force on you are these normal forces pushing you up. So you are accelerating upwards, but I'm not moving up. Relative to what? I mean, relative to the flip chart and the floor and basically everything in this room, but all of those things are in your frame of reference, which you know is not inertial.
cues.zh: 你没有重量，所以作用在你身上的唯一力就是这些向上的支持力。所以你在向上加速，但我并没有向上移。相对于什么？我是说，相对于挂图、地板以及这个房间里的基本上所有东西，但所有这些东西都在你的参考系里，而你知道这个参考系是非惯性系。

cues.en: Relative to everything in my rocket ship, I'm not accelerating.
cues.zh: 相对于我飞船里的所有东西，我并没有在加速。

cues.en: What you need if you really wanna measure your acceleration is someone in an inertial frame of reference, like the guy who fell off the roof.
cues.zh: 如果你真的想测量你的加速度，你需要的是一个处于惯性参考系中的人，比如那个从屋顶掉下去的人。

cues.en: And he would see you accelerating up at 9.8 meters per second squared.
cues.zh: 他会看到你以每秒每秒 9.8 米的加速度向上加速。

cues.en: I think what this shows is that what an acceleration really is is it's a deviation
cues.zh: 我认为这说明了加速度的本质其实是一种偏差

cues.en: from a geodesic.
cues.zh: 背离了测地线。

cues.en: You can't follow a straight line path through space time because the floor prevents you from doing that. It applies a force upwards on you, so you're accelerating up.
cues.zh: 你无法沿着一条直线穿过时空，因为地板阻止了你这样做。它对你施加了一个向上的力，所以你在向上加速。

cues.en: But if I'm accelerating up and so is everyone else around the world and presumably the whole surface of the Earth, then shouldn't the Earth be expanding?
cues.zh: 但如果我在向上加速，世界上的其他人也是如此，大概整个地球表面也是如此，那地球难道不应该在膨胀吗？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不。

cues.en: It is possible for you to be accelerating
cues.zh: 你是有可能处于加速状态的

cues.en: even though your spatial coordinates are not changing.
cues.zh: 即使你的空间坐标并没有改变。

cues.en: I will show you one equation from general relativity.
cues.zh: 我将向你们展示广义相对论中的一个方程。

cues.en: This says that the second derivative of your position with respect to time is equal to your acceleration.
cues.zh: 这表明你的位置对时间的二阶导数等于你的加速度。

cues.en: That's just f on m. And if you were in flat space time, well, this is exactly what you're saying. If you're accelerating, your spatial coordinates have to change.
cues.zh: 这其实就是 F 除以 m。如果你在平直时空中，没错，正如你所说，只要你在加速，你的空间坐标就必然会改变。

cues.en: But you're not in flat space time,
cues.zh: 但你并不在平直时空中，

cues.en: and this term is related to the curvature of space time, and this is your velocity through time squared.
cues.zh: 而这一项与时空曲率有关，这一项是你穿越时间速度的平方。

cues.en: You don't have to worry about the details here. The point is
cues.zh: 这里不用太纠结细节，重点在于

cues.en: your position can be not changing. This can be zero,
cues.zh: 你的位置可以保持不变，这一项可以为零，

cues.en: which means your acceleration
cues.zh: 这意味着你的加速度

cues.en: must be exactly
cues.zh: 必须刚好

cues.en: equal to
cues.zh: 等于

cues.en: this this curvature term times your velocity through time squared.
cues.zh: 这个……这个曲率项乘以你穿越时间速度的平方。

cues.en: So in curved spacetime,
cues.zh: 所以在弯曲时空中，

cues.en: you need to accelerate
cues.zh: 你必须加速

cues.en: just to stand still.
cues.zh: 仅仅是为了保持静止。

cues.en: A lot of this may seem more complicated than Newtonian physics, but one classical mystery looks a whole lot simpler in general relativity,
cues.zh: 这些听起来可能比牛顿力学复杂得多，但在广义相对论中，有一个经典谜题却变得简单多了，

cues.en: which is why all objects fall at the same rate.
cues.zh: 那就是为什么所有物体下落的速度都一样。

cues.en: They are at the same times.
cues.zh: 它们在同一时间落地。

cues.en: I have made a number of videos on this topic and I would always give the standard Newtonian explanation.
cues.zh: 我做过很多关于这个话题的视频，以前我总是给出标准的牛顿力学解释。

cues.en: The only force on a free falling body is its weight, g m m on r squared, which equals its mass times acceleration.
cues.zh: 自由落体受到的唯一力就是重力，即 G M m 除以 r 的平方，等于质量乘以加速度。

cues.en: You can cancel the object's mass on both sides of the equation, hence, all objects will have this same acceleration.
cues.zh: 你可以消掉方程两边的物体质量，因此，所有物体都会获得相同的加速度。

cues.en: The mystery is why we could cancel these two m's.
cues.zh: 谜团在于：为什么我们可以消掉这两个 m？

cues.en: The one on the left was gravitational mass, the property of an object that creates and experiences a gravitational field,
cues.zh: 左边的是引力质量，代表物体产生和感受引力场的特性，

cues.en: while the m on the right is inertial mass, a measure of resistance to acceleration.
cues.zh: 而右边的 m 则是惯性质量，代表物体抵抗加速度的能力。

cues.en: Why should these two conceptually different properties
cues.zh: 为什么这两个概念上不同的属性

cues.en: be numerically
cues.zh: 在数值上

cues.en: identical?
cues.zh: 会完全相同？

cues.en: Scientists have spent a lot of time and effort experimentally testing down to around one part in 10,000,000,000,000
cues.zh: 科学家花了大量时间和精力做实验，精度达到大约十万亿分之一

cues.en: that these two types of mass really are the same.
cues.zh: 来验证这两种质量确实相同。

cues.en: But in general relativity,
cues.zh: 但在广义相对论中，

cues.en: there is no mystery.
cues.zh: 这并不神秘。

cues.en: All objects appear to fall the same way because they're not accelerating.
cues.zh: 所有物体看起来都以相同方式下落，是因为它们并没有在加速。

cues.en: They're just following straight line paths through space time until they encounter something that stops them.
cues.zh: 它们只是在时空中沿直线路径运动，直到遇到东西把它们挡住。

cues.en: Like the objects in the rocket ship, they appear to accelerate at the same rate because they're not really accelerating. It's the floor accelerating into them.
cues.zh: 就像火箭飞船里的物体，它们看起来以相同速率加速，是因为它们其实没有加速。是地板朝它们加速撞上来。

cues.en: Now, a lot of this might seem pretty far fetched as it did back in 1915 when Einstein proposed it. So he very cleverly came up with a measurable prediction that scientists could make to test his theory.
cues.zh: 现在，这些听起来可能很牵强，就像 1915 年爱因斯坦提出时一样。所以他很聪明地提出了一个可测量的预测，让科学家能检验他的理论。

cues.en: Imagine that this rocket ship is coasting through deep space.
cues.zh: 想象这艘火箭飞船正滑行在深空中。

cues.en: If you shine a light beam across the rocket ship, well, it'll do exactly what you expect. Light travels in a straight line and hits a point on the opposite wall at exactly the same height as the source.
cues.zh: 如果你让一束光横穿火箭飞船，它会完全如你所料。光沿直线传播，打在对面墙上与光源完全相同高度的点。

cues.en: But now, what if this rocket is accelerating?
cues.zh: 但现在，如果这艘火箭正在加速呢？

cues.en: Well, to an external observer, they're still gonna see the same thing, light traveling in a straight line.
cues.zh: 对外部观察者来说，他们仍会看到同样的情况：光沿直线传播。

cues.en: But inside the rocket,
cues.zh: 但在火箭内部，

cues.en: during the time it takes the light to travel across the cabin,
cues.zh: 在光穿过舱室所需的时间里，

cues.en: the rocket will have sped up. So by the time it hits the other wall,
cues.zh: 火箭已经加速了。所以当光打到另一面墙时，

cues.en: it'll hit a little lower than before.
cues.zh: 会打在比之前稍低的位置。

cues.en: So in an accelerating frame of reference, light deflects down.
cues.zh: 所以在加速参考系中，光线会向下偏折。

cues.en: Here, I am dramatically exaggerating the effect. Even if I were accelerating up at 10 g's, which would probably kill me, the deflection would be on the order of the width of a proton.
cues.zh: 这里我大幅夸大了效果。就算我以10个g的加速度上升，那大概会要了我的命，偏移量也不过是质子宽度那么点。

cues.en: Still,
cues.zh: 即便如此，

cues.en: it shows
cues.zh: 它展示了

cues.en: that an accelerating frame of reference will bend light.
cues.zh: 加速参考系会使光线发生弯曲。

cues.en: So Einstein reasoned, light must also bend when it passes a large mass.
cues.zh: 所以爱因斯坦推断，光在通过巨大质量时也必定会发生弯曲。

cues.en: But where do you find a mass large enough?
cues.zh: 但你又去哪里找一个质量足够大的物体呢？

cues.en: Well, the only obvious
cues.zh: 嗯，唯一的明显

cues.en: huge mass near the earth is the sun.
cues.zh: 靠近地球的巨大质量体就是太阳。

cues.en: So the ideal experiment would be to look at light passing just next to the sun and see if it is deflected.
cues.zh: 所以理想的实验，是观察从太阳近旁经过的光，看它是否会发生偏折。

cues.en: Say, light from distant stars.
cues.zh: 比如说，来自遥远恒星的光。

cues.en: The problem was, of course, the sun is just so bright you can't see stars right next to it unless
cues.zh: 问题当然在于，太阳实在是太亮了，以至于你根本看不到它身旁的星星，除非

cues.en: there is a total solar eclipse,
cues.zh: 发生了一次日全食，

cues.en: which is exactly what happened in 1919.
cues.zh: 这正是 1919 年发生的事情。

cues.en: So Arthur Eddington set out to take pictures of the stars right next to the sun during
cues.zh: 于是 Arthur Eddington 着手在……期间拍摄紧挨太阳的恒星照片

cues.en: totality.
cues.zh: 总体性。

cues.en: And what he found by analyzing those pictures was that their positions appeared deflected by the precise amount predicted by Einstein's
cues.zh: 通过对这些照片的分析，他发现它们的位置发生了偏转，其偏转程度与爱因斯坦预测的完全一致

cues.en: general theory of relativity.
cues.zh: 广义相对论。

cues.en: The result was twice the deflection some had calculated using a strictly Newtonian model. And general relativity has passed virtually every test put to it over the past hundred years or so. But there are still more things to try.
cues.zh: 这一结果是某些人仅凭牛顿模型计算出的偏折量的两倍。而在过去一百多年里，广义相对论几乎通过了对它的每一次检验。但我们仍有更多测试可以去尝试。

cues.en: A well known and empirically validated finding is that accelerating charges radiate electromagnetic
cues.zh: 一个众所周知且经过实证验证的发现是，加速电荷会辐射电磁波

cues.en: radiation.
cues.zh: 辐射。

cues.en: So one conceptually simple experimental test would be to compare the behavior of a stationary charge in a gravitational field to a free falling one. If a more Newtonian picture of gravity is correct, well, then the stationary charge should not radiate electromagnetic radiation,
cues.zh: 所以，一个概念上很简单的实验，就是比较引力场中静止电荷和自由落体电荷的行为。如果牛顿式的引力图景是正确的，那么静止电荷就不应发出电磁辐射，

cues.en: but a free falling one is accelerating, and therefore, it should radiate.
cues.zh: 但自由落体电荷正在加速，因此应该会发出辐射。

cues.en: In contrast,
cues.zh: 相比之下，

cues.en: general relativity sees
cues.zh: 广义相对论认为

cues.en: the free falling charge as non accelerating. It's just going on a straight line path through curved space time, whereas the stationary charge is accelerating, and therefore, it should give off electromagnetic radiation.
cues.zh: 自由落体电荷并没有加速。它只是在弯曲时空中沿直线运动，而静止电荷才是在加速，因此应该会发出电磁辐射。

cues.en: Now, thus far, logistical challenges have prevented anyone from actually carrying out this experiment,
cues.zh: 不过到目前为止，实际执行这个实验的后勤难题一直阻碍着所有人，

cues.en: but what you believe will happen reveals what you truly think about the nature of gravity.
cues.zh: 但你认为实验会发生什么，恰恰揭示了你对引力本质的真实看法。

cues.en: Do you think that a freely falling charge will radiate electromagnetic radiation
cues.zh: 你认为自由落体电荷会发出电磁辐射

cues.en: or not?
cues.zh: 还是不会？

cues.en: Is gravity an illusion?
cues.zh: 引力是一种幻觉吗？

cues.en: This episode was sponsored by Caseta, and so I used the sponsorship money,
cues.zh: 本期节目由 Caseta 赞助，所以我用赞助费

cues.en: to have a rocket ship built.
cues.zh: 造了一艘火箭飞船。

cues.en: Caseta by Lutron makes these smart light switches in the rocket ship. They also make remotes, motion sensors, smart plugs, basically every smart switch you could use for turning things in your home on and off.
cues.zh: Caseta by Lutron 在这艘火箭飞船里安装了智能灯开关。他们还生产遥控器、运动传感器、智能插座，基本上你家里用来开关设备的智能开关，他们都有。

cues.en: But installing a smart switch isn't rocket science. Just turn off the power to the switch, detach the existing wires, and reconnect them to the Caseta smart switch. What's great about smart switches as opposed to smart bulbs is one switch often controls multiple bulbs, So you can save money by replacing only the switch. And they connect to most smart devices like Alexa, Google Assistant, and Apple HomeKit.
cues.zh: 不过，安装智能开关并不是什么火箭科学。只要先关闭开关的电源，拆下原有电线，再把它们接回 Caseta 智能开关即可。智能开关比智能灯泡更棒的一点是，一个开关通常能控制多个灯泡，所以你只需更换开关，就能省下不少钱。它们还能连接 Alexa、Google Assistant 和 Apple HomeKit 等大多数智能设备。

cues.en: And you can control them via an app on your phone.
cues.zh: 你还可以通过手机上的 App 来控制它们。

cues.en: So if you forget to turn off the lights in the rocket, no need to go back, just turn them off in the app. You could also use the app to set up schedules,
cues.zh: 所以，如果你忘记关火箭里的灯，也不用跑回去，直接在 App 上关掉就行。你还可以用 App 设置定时，

cues.en: turning the lights on when it goes dark.
cues.zh: 天黑时自动开灯。

cues.en: This gives you peace of mind knowing your family will always come home to a well lit house. Now we may not have personal rockets yet, but we have smart switches and the smart choice for these devices is Caseta by Lutron.
cues.zh: 这让您安心无忧，家人回家时总能看到一个灯火通明的家。虽然我们现在还没有私人火箭，但我们有智能开关，而这些设备的智能之选就是路创（Lutron）的 Caseta。
